hook: Most drones shatter on impact, but this one keeps flying at 25 km/h.

sections.voiceover: Most drones shatter on impact, but this one keeps flying at 25 km/h.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of the FlexiQuad drone frame deforming against a wall.
sections.sfx_cue: Sharp impact sound followed by the steady hum of rotors.
b_roll: ETH Zurich laboratory footage showing the FlexiQuad collision test

sections.voiceover: How does the FlexiQuad frame protect the 3-cell batteries while maintaining flight after impact?
sections.visual_cue: Diagram showing the four FR-4 fiberglass strips forming the circular drone frame.
sections.sfx_cue: Mechanical clicking sounds transitioning into an airy, high-tech tone.
b_roll: Close-up technical render of the FR-4 fiberglass composite structure

sections.voiceover: Instead, ETH Zurich places a 330 mAh 3-cell battery directly under each motor.
sections.visual_cue: Highlighting the battery placement under the motor mounts on the frame.
sections.sfx_cue: Electronic ping sound highlighting the battery locations.
b_roll: Close-up of the battery modules attached to the FlexiQuad frame

sections.voiceover: Luca Girardi, Gabriel Maquignaz, and Stefano Mintchev published this bioinspired study in November 2025. The FlexiQuad recovers control after collisions because of its 0.5 mm thick fiberglass strips.
sections.visual_cue: Side-by-side shot of the drone hitting an obstacle and immediately stabilizing.
sections.sfx_cue: Whoosh sound followed by the stable drone motor hum.
b_roll: Slow-motion footage of the FlexiQuad colliding and stabilizing

sections.voiceover: That flexible ring frame withstands speeds of 25 km/h.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the FlexiQuad drone hovering steadily after impact.
sections.sfx_cue: Fade out of the rotor hum.
b_roll: FlexiQuad drone flying in the ETH Zurich laboratory
